requirements.requirement: Create the shared identity dataops with UID and GID 4500 on both nodes, and configure the shared directory as dataops:dataops with mode 2770.
requirements.summary: Both nodes directly report dataops as UID/GID 4500. The exported directory and its mounted representation report ownership 4500:4500 and mode 2770, including after both node restarts.

requirements.requirement: Export /srv/nfs/shared from node1 and mount that share at /mnt/shared on node2.
requirements.summary: The server export is active and limited to node2, while node2 directly reports an NFSv4.1 mount from the required source at /mnt/shared. Export and mount both recovered after their respective node restarts.

requirements.requirement: Ensure files created from either system retain consistent ownership and permissions.
requirements.summary: Files and directories created as dataops from both nodes were visible from the opposite node with dataops:dataops ownership; files had mode 660 and directories inherited group ownership and mode 2770. Reads and new writes also succeeded after both restarts.

requirements.requirement: Retain the installed operating-system release and kernel, using software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: Both nodes remained RHEL 7.9 with kernel 3.10.0-1160.el7.x86_64 before and after execution. EL7 nfs-utils 1.3.0 packages were installed and demonstrated working across restarts.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct behavioral evidence. The provider-wide restart protocol is also complete for both nodes: each has a healthy pre-restart state, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity corroborated by lifecycle observations, and recovered service, mount, data, ownership, and write behavior.
limitations: The lifecycle package-health checks timed out both before and after execution, so package-manager consistency lacks an independent global cross-check despite successful package transactions and runtime behavior.
Lifecycle snapshots are generic and do not independently inspect the NFS export, mount, identities, or permissions; those outcomes rely on the detailed executor command evidence.

operational_hygiene.summary: The implementation was narrowly scoped, left no failed services, restricted server firewall access to node2, and retained only task-relevant services and configuration. Two low-risk residue classes remained: temporary downloaded GPG-key files created during package setup were left on both nodes (cmd-481a4aa214b44ee5, cmd-4f3eff9d24f24f55), and reboot log files created by the mandatory restart commands were left in /tmp on both nodes (cmd-cd80e058a3634829, cmd-05e6174883374522). These artifacts were not needed after completion and were not reverted. No other unnecessary mutation is established by the trace; test data mutations had a clear bounded verification and recovery-evidence role.
